audit_2026_10_18.verdict: PASS — identity measured on the full trailing-12-month window before build (174,123 rows -> 147,687 issuance events; see dedupe_rule); dataset updated 2026-10-17 (daily). PHASE1-PLAN secondary list, first in line.

coverage_note: New York City Department of Buildings (DOB NOW) permits for this borough only. The DOB NOW: Build feed is citywide; each NYC borough is a county and gets its own county report. DOB NOW excludes electrical, elevator, and limited-alteration (LAA) permits, which DOB publishes in separate datasets — they are not in this feed.

dedupe_rule.definition: A 'permit' for New York City = one DOB NOW permit ISSUANCE EVENT: one (job_filing_number, tracking_number) pair. The feed's grain is one row per work type an issuance covers, so a single issuance appears as 1-6 rows that agree on every other field; the pipeline collapses those rows into one record whose trade set is the issuance's work types. permit_number = work_permit (the permit slot's public number, e.g. B01241382-I1-GC); the same slot is issued repeatedly over time (initial + renewals), and each issuance is its own permit record — the same treatment Chicago/Austin records get, where a renewal is a separate issued permit. Identity validity condition: a real DOB job filing number matches [borough letter][8 digits]-[iteration] (125,096 of 125,097 distinct window job numbers). The single exception is the feed's own placeholder text 'Permit is no' (work_permit 'Permit is not yet issued') on 4 window events — renewals whose filing number DOB did not carry into the feed. With no real source identity they are HELD at normalization, reported, never published.
dedupe_rule.measurement_2026_10_18: Trailing-12-month issue window (issued_date >= 2025-10-17), measured on the full pulled window before build: 174,123 rows -> 147,687 distinct (job_filing_number, tracking_number) events. Every event carries exactly ONE distinct work_permit (147,687 of 147,687), and ZERO events disagree internally on issued_date, permit_status, borough, estimated_job_costs, applicant_business_name, or filing_reason. Rows per event = covered work types (1 for 129,760 events; max 6). Events per work_permit slot: 115,602 slots issued once in the window, max 8 issuances. tracking_number ALONE is not an identity: 51 (tracking_number, work_type) groups window-wide are collisions between unrelated jobs in different boroughs, which is why the key includes job_filing_number. filing_reason mix (events): Initial Permit 95,010 (64.3%), Renewal Without Changes 40,976 (27.7%), Renewal with Changes 10,690 (7.2%), 'No Work Permit' 644 and missing 367 (both carry ordinary issued slots; the counting rule does not depend on the reason label).
dedupe_rule.rule: source_record_id = job_filing_number + '|' + tracking_number. Collapse happens in the pipeline (registry collapse_events) before normalization; the in-batch duplicate gate and the DB upsert key remain as guards.
dedupe_rule.valuation_warning: estimated_job_costs is a JOB-FILING-level figure restated identically on every issuance event of the filing (17,486 of 17,487 multi-event filings state one identical cost on all their events). Summing per event ($58,825,802,894) counts one filing's cost up to 8 times. See field_map.valuation for the per-filing attribution rule that makes values publishable.

field_map.application_date: approved_date — the filing's DOB approval date. This feed publishes no application-submission date; approval is the pre-issuance date DOB reports, carried in the application-date field and labeled as approval in the registry so the mapping is never mistaken for a submission date.
field_map.category: none — DOB NOW publishes no residential/commercial class for a permit; honest NULL (SF/Chicago precedent)
field_map.contractor_rule: applicant_business_name ONLY — the business name of the licensed professional/permittee of record (permittee_s_license_type is predominantly GC and other licensed trades). The dataset deliberately separates applicant_first_name/middle_name/last_name (the person) from applicant_business_name (the business): the person fields, all filing_representative_* fields, and all owner_* fields (owner_name is a person; owner_business_name is the property owner, not the contractor) are EXCLUDED from pull_select, so they are never requested from the API at all. Business-name coverage: 99.6% of rows all-time; NULL where unpublished, never inferred.
field_map.permit_number: work_permit — the permit slot's public number (job number + discipline suffix, e.g. B01241382-I1-GC). A slot recurs across its issuance events (initial + renewals).
field_map.permit_type_source: the issuance's work types joined (work_type values, e.g. 'General Construction; Plumbing') — DOB NOW work types are the feed's own permit categories
field_map.project_description: job_description (constant within an issuance event; first row carried)
field_map.source_record_id: job_filing_number + '|' + tracking_number (one DOB NOW issuance event — see dedupe_rule; measured unique on the full window, 2026-10-18)
field_map.valuation: estimated_job_costs — a per-job-filing estimate restated on each of the filing's issuance events. PUBLICATION RULE (measured 2026-10-18): each filing's stated cost is attributed ONCE, to the filing's LATEST issuance event in the window (by issued_date, then tracking_number); the filing's earlier events in the window store NULL. Per-filing totals on that rule: $43,586,788,485 across 125,097 filings window-wide (vs $58,825,802,894 naive per-event). Coverage: all 147,687 events parse numerically; 17,553 events state $0 and 3,319 state $1 (applicants' own figures, carried as reported). Among real filings, none states conflicting costs: a server-side GROUP BY over the window finds exactly one cost per (filing, borough) pair for all 125,096 real filings (the only multi-cost 'filing' is the placeholder 'Permit is no', whose 4 events are held). Published borough totals were verified to the cent against that independent GROUP BY sum (citywide $43,586,788,485). 6,785 events state costs with cents; published figures round to the dollar. Filing-level coverage: 14,703 filings state $0 and 2,273 state $1 (applicants' own figures, carried as reported); 86.4% of filings state more than $1. The rule and its evidence are printed on the Data Sources page.
field_map.work_type_source: work_type set of the issuance + job_description (dedicated classifier pass: trades.classify_nyc_trade)
